## 4. Quantitative perturbation theorem with an arbitrarily fast bath

In the known-site configuration, suppose a unitary core is generated by

\[
H(t)=I_{F_j}\otimes H_{DM}(t)+V(t),\qquad
\operatorname{Tr}_{F_j} V(t)=0,\quad
\varepsilon=\int_0^T\|V(t)\|dt. \tag{10}
\]

`H_DM(t)` may be arbitrarily large and noncommuting at different times. In the `H_DM` interaction picture, `Tr_j V_I(t)=0`. Duhamel expansion with unitary remainder gives

\[
\left\|B_0-U_{DM}(T)\right\|\le\frac{\varepsilon^2}{2}, \qquad
\sum_{a\ne I}B_a^\dagger B_a\preceq\varepsilon^2 I. \tag{11}
\]

The first inequality is the absent identity coefficient of the *first-order* Dyson term. The second bounds amplitude leaving the code before syndrome correction. For the deterministic corrected channel `N_recovered(ρ)=Σ_a B_a ρ B_a†` and unperturbed `U0(ρ)=U_DM ρ U_DM†`, even with arbitrary references,

\[
\boxed{\tfrac12\|\mathcal N_{\mathrm{recovered}}-\mathcal U_0\|_\diamond
\le \min(1,\varepsilon^2).} \tag{12}
\]

This is a full data-plus-bath accuracy guarantee, not just flag privacy or a small observed output marginal. **The bound uses only the local coupling norm, not the bath bandwidth**, and does not label its residual as an exact stochastic fault process in an uncorrected circuit.

FOUR-SPIN CORRECTABLE ACCESS
P=(I+XXXX)(I+ZZZZ)/4 has rank4. Every nonidentity single-site Pauli anticommutes with a stabilizer, hence P sigma_j P=0. These equalities give the one-site marginal I_j/2 tensor rho_R for every encoded logical/reference state: coefficients against each traceless single-site Pauli vanish, while the identity coefficient is rho_R. This is privacy from the exposed spin, not independence of the data from the bath.
For a fixed known j, P_a=sigma_j^a P sigma_j^a are orthogonal and sum to I. For completed K_lambda=sum_a sigma_j^a tensor B_a,lambda, trusted syndrome extraction and correction give sigma_j^a P_a K_lambda P=P tensor B_a,lambda. Every retained syndrome/report branch acts identically on the logical flag and as an arbitrary CP map on data plus memory. Logical preframes can therefore be followed by that recovery, late key readout/retirement and matched output correction, yielding the existing positive Pauli/pre-T and destructive-test instruments separately for each retained syndrome. This does not certify data quality or useful throughput.
For unknown exposure, the completed Kraus LINEAR SPAN identity plus weight-one Paulis suffices for PKP=P tensor B0. Syndrome++ postselection gives an accepted branch but can reject every permitted attempt. Do not silently retry a consumed unknown payload. Knowing that only one site is touched at each instant is weaker: products across times can have weight two. Z1Z2 is a nontrivial logical observable, so two sequential contacts can learn a key parity while passing both stabilizers. X1 and X2 also share a syndrome and cannot both be corrected at unknown location by this distance-two code. Earlier exact twirl theorems survive at their original narrower boundary.
In H=I_F tensor H_DM+V with V on known j and Tr_j V=0, set epsilon=int||V||. In the interaction picture, the identity coefficient of the first Dyson term vanishes; ||B0-U_DM||<=epsilon^2/2. Leakage norm before recovery is<=epsilon, so sum_nonzero B_a dagger B_a<=epsilon^2 I. The good-Kraus channel difference has diamond norm<=2||B0-U_DM|| (B0 and U are contractions); bad branches have diamond norm<=epsilon^2. Half-diamond error<=min(1,epsilon^2), on the full data/bath/reference channel. This bound does not require a bath speed bound, and does not invent exact stochastic labels for an approximate reference comparison.
